Mir Fateh Ali ------ Petitioner
Vs. 
Alhaj Mohammad Minajuddin & anr ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was directed against the judgment and decree dated 18-3-90 and 25-3-90 respectively passed by Subordinate Judge, Shariatpur in Title Appeal No. 72 of 1989 reversing the judgment and decree dated 15-3-89 and 22-3-89 respectively passed by Assistant Judge, Danudeya in Other Class Suit No. 68 of 1983.

2. The short facts giving rise to this Rule may be stated as follows:

Opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiff instituted title suit No.190 of 1983 in the court of Chikundi, District Shariatpur for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and for demarcating the suit land and that the suit was subsequently transferred to the court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge) at Damudeya and re-numbered as Other Class Suit No. 68 of 1983. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the land of RS plot No. 520 covering 032 decimals of land as described in the schedule to the plaint originally belonged to one Obhoy Charan Shil who transferred the land to one Wahab Ali Matbar and Jonab Ali Matbar from whom the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 purchased the same by 2 (two) registered kabalas dated 6-12-56 and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by constructing huts and growing trees therein. To the adjacent south of this plot 520 stands plot No. 529 belonging to the defendant which is a tank. That 0.5 decimals of land of the plaintiff''s plot No. 520 was broken down by natural decay and merged with defendant''s tank plot No. 529 and that another 0.3 decimals of land of the plaintiffs' plot is merged with the northern bank of the defendant''s tank. Thus a total of decimals of land of plaintiffs' plot No. 520 has entered into the defendant plot No. 529. The plaintiffs have got their right, title and possession in this decimal of land, but the defendant has denied the title of the plaintiffs in respect of this 0.8 decimals of land and threatened them to cut away the trees there from in Chaitra, 1389 BS. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for raising a pucca pillar by the boundary of the plaintiffs and defendant''s land.

3. The defendant contested the suit by filing a written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable, that the suit is bad for defect of party and that the suit is barred by limitation. The defendant''s case is that he has no claim over the plaintiffs'' plot No. 520 and that no land of the plaintiffs'' plot has been merged with the defendant''s plot No. 529 and that the plaintiffs have no cause of action for this suit.

4. The learned Assistant Judge after considering the facts and evidence of this case found that the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable and that no land of the plaintiffs' plot No. 520 has been merged with the defendant''s plot No. 529, with this and other findings the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the plaintiffs' suit by his judgment and decree dated 15-3-89 and 22-3-89. Against that judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge, the plaintiffs filed title Appeal No. 72 of 1989 in the court of District Judge which was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, Shariatpur. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing both the parties, allowed the appeal, reversed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff vide his judgment and decree dated 18-3-90 and 25-3-90 respectively.

5. Being aggrieved by this judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, the defendant No. 1 as petitioner has moved this court and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr. Enamul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioner, has submitted that the plaintiff''s suit was not maintainable in its present form and that the measurement of the land as made by the Advocate Commissioner was wrong and that the learned Assistant Judge after discussing and considering all this aspects of the matter had rightly dismissed the suit, but that the learned Subordinate Judge without making proper appreciation of the facts and evidence of the case has illegally reversed the findings of the learned Assistant Judge by the impugned judgment and thereby the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law resulting in an error in his decision.

7. Mr. Shaheed Alam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite parties, has, on the other hand, it italic that the learned Advocate commissioner by his survey measurement found the suit land to have been merged with the defendant''s plot No. 529 and that the learned Subordinate Judge by considering this survey report together with oral evidence came to his correct finding and rightly decreed the suit.

8. It appears that admittedly the suit plot No. 520 belongs to the plaintiffs and the adjacent southern plot No. 529 which is a tank belongs to the defendant. The plaintiffs'' case is that the 0.5 decimals of land of their plot No. 520 has been merged with the watery portion of the defendant''s tank by natural decay and 0.3 decimals are there in the bank of the tank and, as such, the plaintiffs filed the suit for demarcating the boundary by raising a pucca pillar and for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in respect of this total decimals of land. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge framed an issue to the effect that whether the suit was maintainable in its present form and after considering the evidence of the case he found that the suit was not maintainable. The learned Subordinate Judge also framed such an issue and observed that the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and for demarcating the boundary pillar which means that the plaintiffs filed the suit for the partition. But it is not stated by the learned Subordinate Judge as to what kind of partition it is. Partition always means division and allotment of saham of an ejmali property. But the admitted facts of the instant case are that the suit plot 520 and adjacent defendant''s plot No. 529 are not the ejmali property. These are the two separate plots separately possessed by two different owners having no connection with each other. Therefore, this view of the learned Subordinate Judge apparently appears to be a wrong approach to the whole matter.

9. Mr. Enamul Huq, the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner, next argued that the suit is again not maintainable in view of the fact that although the Advocate Commissioner submitted a survey report but that report is not a correct report in view of the fact that the Advocate Commissioner did not measure both the plots to find out whether the alleged 0.8 decimals of plaintiff''s land has been merged into defendants plot No. 529 and for that and for other reasons, the learned Assistant Judge has correctly found the Advocate Commissioner''s report to be a wrong one, but that the learned Subordinate Judge did not make any proper assessment of the Advocate Commissioner''s report and came to an erroneous finding in that respect.

10. Mr. Shahid Alam in this respect submits that the report of the Advocate Commissioner has been accepted by the court vide order No. 65 in the record and as such the court cannot come to a different finding from his own order No. 65. The contention of Mr. Enamul Huq in this respect is that the court can consider the report with reference to the evidence as may be adduced by the parties at the time of trial of the suit and in this connection Mr. Huq referred to a decision in the case of Abul Quasem (Md) vs. Md Lutfur Rahman reported in 43 DLR (AD) 17 wherein their Lordships have observed as follows:

"Commissioner's report is to be evaluated in the facts of the case on the evidence adduced and the court has wide discretion in such matter. Mere acceptance of the report should not give rise to any apprehension in the mind of the litigant."

11. By a reading of the order No. 65 dated 21-12-88 of the instant case before me, it appears that the learned Assistant Judge has stated in his order that he considered the commissioners report, field book covering 24 pages and map and then accepted the report. It apparently appears from this order that the learned Assistant Judge did not examine the commissioner to prove his report nor did he give any chance to the defendant to cross-examine the Advocate Commissioner and thus it appears that the normal procedure necessary, for acceptance of commissioner's report was not at all followed. It further appears that there is no order whether the objection against the commissioner's report was rejected or not. Therefore, this kind of acceptance of the commissioner''s report cannot be considered to be a decision of fact in issue. Court, therefore, shall have all the power to evaluate the commissioner's report on the basis of the evidence as adduced by the parties in court during trial of the suit. Thus it appears that the learned Assistant Judge had evaluated the commissioner''s report during the trial of the suit on the basis of the evidence of the witness according to the principle of law as laid down in the decision referred to above.

<u>12. Mr. Enamul Huq, next submits that the commissioner started his work from a different village of a different police station and that the defendant's direct objection was that the commissioner did not come to the locality and that the commissioner was directed to start his survey work from a pillar within the suit village, but he has not done so. From order No. 65 of the record, it appears that the commissioner's field book covers 24 pages. Thus it appears that the commissioner's field book is not only an unusual field book but also it appears that the commissioner has unnecessarily travelled a long way to make a show of survey only. The commissioner did not say whether he found any fixed pillar within the suit village. It further appears that he did not measure both the plots to locate the boundary of the disputed plots.</u>

13. Under all the above facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that the learned Assistant Judge has correctly evaluated the commissioner''s report and found it to have not reflected the proper position of the land. But from the impugned judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge it appears that there was a total non-consideration of all these facts, circumstances and evidence of the case. In that view of the matter, I find that the decision of the learned Subordinate Judge in this respect is not based on proper assessment of the facts and materials on record.

14. The whole case of the plaintiff''s is that they have lost decimals of land by the southern side of their plot No. 520 five decimals of which has been merged in the watery portion and 3 decimals of which has been merged in the bank of the tank by the northern side of the defendant''s tank plot No. 529. But it appears that the plaintiffs did not make any prayer in their plaint for recovery of this decimal of land from defendant's plot but that they have prayed for confirmation of possession in this land only. It is not understood how he can possess this decimals of land in defendant's tank plot No. 529 without recovery of possession there from. It will remain a part of the tank until it is recovered but it appears that the plaintiffs did not make any prayer for recovery of possession.

15. In view of the above circumstances, it appears that the factum of possession of the suit land was a matter for the courts below to decide. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge has discussed the evidence of possession of the suit land quite elaborately. The learned Assistant Judge has stated in his judgment that the plaintiff as PW 1 has said in his cross examination that the land which is in the schedule of his kabala has been purchased by him. Learned Assistant Judge has discussed in his judgment that the plaintiffs' plot is plot No. 520 and that there is no tank in that plot and that none of the PWs have said whether any land of his plot No. 520 was broken by rain, cyclone or flood to merge with defendants plot No. 529 and thus the learned Assistant Judge came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs'' claim of merger of decimal of land of his plot No 520 with defendant''s plot No 529 and of plaintiffs'' claim of possession therein have not been proved at all. Obviously, without cultivating any fish the plaintiffs cannot claim any possession in somebody else''s tank.

16. If the plaintiffs have any land or decimals of land in the tank plot of the defendant, then they should have made a prayer to recover possession and then to make boundary pillar. But it appears that the plaintiffs have not done so. The learned Subordinate Judge observed in his judgment that the defendant has no claim in plot No. 520 and since 8 decimals of land of this plot has been merged in plot No. 529, so it can be naturally said that the plaintiffs are in possession of this 8 decimals of land. But it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge has made a fallacious observation without the basis of any evidence in that respect, firstly, because the merger is only a claim of the plaintiffs, but it has not been proved by evidence and secondly, because if the decimals of land is washed away from plaintiff's plot No. 520 as alleged and merged with some other land, then the question of plaintiffs' possession in that washed away land does not arise. I have found above that the learned Assistant Judge has discussed and considered the evidence of the witness and came to the finding that the plaintiffs' claim of possession has not been proved. But the finding of possession as arrived at by the learned Subordinate Judge is not based on any evidence nor on proper appreciation of actual facts and materials on record.

<u>17. By a careful consideration of all the above facts and circumstances and the position of the case, I find that the impugned judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge is not based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case nor proper appreciation of the evidence on record. I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal. I, therefore, find that the learned Subordinate judge has committed an error resulting in an error of law in his decision which has occasioned a failure of justice to the defendant-petitioner. The impugned judgment, in my opinion, suffers from infirmity. Hence it calls for interference by this court.</u>

For all the reasons stated above, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge are hereby set aside and those passed by the learned Assistant Judge are restored.

End.

parties:
Jahangir Alam (Md) and another ----- Appellant
Vs.
Md. Shamsur Rah-J man Sarder & others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 24-8-2002 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.408 of 2002.)
full_judgment:
SK Sinha J: These appeals by leave is directed from the judgment and order dated 24th August, 2002 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.408 of 2002 making the rule absolute and declaring the memo dated 15th January, 2002 of the writ respondent No.2, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

2. The dispute relates to a piece of land appertaining to SA Khatian No.955 of S.A. Khatian No.542 measuring an area of 16 decimals, situates at Bara Moghbazar, Dhaka. The parties are at loggerheads over the ownership of the said land and legal proceedings cropped up since 1961. One Shamsul Huda claiming title of the said plot along with another plot through one Biswanath instituted Title Suit No.170 of 1961 for declaration of title and cancellation of dead No.8142 dated 2nd September, 1961 against Shamsuzzoha Begum in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Bakergonj, Barisal and got an ex-parte decree. According to the writ petitioner said Shamsuzzoha Begum sold the said property to Anis Fatema Begum, the predecessor of interest of the appellant Md. Jahangir Alam suppressing the decree passed in Title Suit No.170 of 1961. One Abdul Wahed Sarder, also instituted Title Suit No.371 of 1991 against aforesaid Anis Fatema and others in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and for further declaration that the deed of Anis Fatema is void, illegal and inoperative. The said suit was also decreed ex-parte on dated 23rd November, 1998. According to the writ petitioner in pursuance of the judgment of the civil Court he has been peacefully possessing the disputed land and filed several petition to the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for mutation of the said land and while his petitions are awaiting decision, he was served with a notice by the writ respondent No.2 of dispossession for implementation of judgment in Writ Petition No.165 of 1998, and he was directed to hand over possession to the Kanoongo which compelled him to institute writ Petition No.408 of 2002 in the High Court Division seeking the above relief. 

3. Appellant in Civil Appeal No.270 of 2003 contested the writ petition by filing an affidavit-in-opposition claiming that the writ petitioner Md. Shamsur Rahman has had no right, title and interest in the disputed property, that the ex-parte decree obtained Abdul Wahed Sarder in Title Suit No.170 of 1961 is void and collusive, that he purchased the disputed property from Anis Fatema by registered deed dated 3rd April, 1987 and thereupon filed Writ Petition No.165 of 1998 seeking a direction upon the Government to release the property from the list of abandoned property and to deliver possession to him, that the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 28th July, 1998 directed the Government including the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to give delivery of possession to him within 2 months from the date of receipt of the judgment and that the decree obtained by Abdul Wahed Sarder in Title Suit No.371 of 1991 is collusive and not binding upon him, inasmuch as, Begum Anis Fatema was not alive when the suit was filed and that he has acquired right, title and interest in the property long before the institution in the said suit. The writ respondent No.2, in the premises, it is claimed, rightly and legally issued the notice upon the writ petitioner with a view to implement the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.165 of 1998. 

4. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 24th August, 2002 made the rule absolute observing as under: 

"In the instant case before us the decision of the civil Court was given in that civil suit (Title Suit No.371 of 1991) which the predecessor-in-interest of the present petitioner (sic)(respondent) was defendant No.1 and the relevant Ministry and the concerned officers were also defendant Nos.2-4. As the question whether the property is abandoned property or not has already been decided in that civil suit, the decision is binding upon the Government. The present petitioner was not made respondent in Writ Petition No.165 of 1998 and it was not brought to the notice of this Court in that writ petition that there is a decision of the Civil Court about the nature of the property which was subject matter of that writ petition. In view of the above position, we are of the view that the petitioner cannot be evicted form the property in question." 

5. Mr. TH Khan, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant contended that the High Court Division on a misconception of law based its decision relying upon the judgment passed in Title Suit No.371 of 1991 in failing to consider that Anis Fatema had no semblance of title when the suit was filed, who was also not alive when the said decree was passed. Mr. Khan further contended that the writ respondent No.2 issued the impugned notice dated 15th January, 2002 in order to give effect to the judgment of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.165 of 1998, in which judgment, the High Court Division, relying upon the Ministry of Land's letter under memo dated 24th August, 1996 approving the decision of the Land Appeal Board releasing the disputed property in favour of Begum Anis Fatema, directed the Deputy Commissioner to effect delivery of possession. It is apparent, as contended, from the said letter that the disputed property is not abandoned property and that the decree passed in Title Suit No.371 of 1991 is not binding upon the appellant. 

6. The High Court Division made the rule absolute relying upon the judgment of the civil 
Court passed in Title Suit No.371 of 1991. This shows that the sheet anchor of the judgment of the High Court Division is the decree passed in Title Suit No.371 of 1991 which is apparently not binding upon the appellant since he was not a party in the suit. The reasons assigned by the High Court Division is absolutely devoid of substance, inasmuch as, the day on which the said suit was instituted Anis Fatema had no right, title and interest in the property. In paragraph 11 of his affidavit-in-opposition the appellant asserted that Anis Fatema had transferred the disputed property in his favour by registered deed dated 2nd April, 1987. In this connection Mr. Khan has taken us to the judgment of the said suit and submits that long before the delivery of the said judgment, Anis Fatema's title has been extinguished. On the strength of this deed he had instituted Writ Petition No.165 of 1998 in the High Court Division and the High Court Division made the rule absolute. Despite those positive statements regarding the acquisition of title by the appellant, the High Court Division observed that the decree is binding upon the appellant as well. 

7. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel appearing for the writ petitioner, while supporting the impugned judgment contended that since Anis Fatema's title was extinguished in pursuance of the judgment passed in Title Suit No.371 of 1991, the High Court Division is perfectly justified in observing that the judgment is also binding upon her successor. We find no basis in the contention of the learned Counsel. 

8. When a judgment is given in evidence, the party against whom it is given in evidence may, in the proceeding in which it is given in evidence, show that the judgment was obtained by fraud or collusion, and a separate suit to have the said judgment set aside is not necessary. In view of the wide terms used in section 44 of the Evidence Act, it cannot be said that it is not open to a Court other than the Court from which the decree was passed, in cases fraud, or collusion, to deal with the matter and decide whether the decree was obtained by fraud or collusion. 

9. The High Court Division though noticed that before the suit was instituted, whatever right, title and interest Anis Fatema had that had been extinguished after execution of deed in 1987 in favour of the appellant, on a misconception of law observed that the said decree is binding upon the appellant. The High Court Division had committed another fundamental error in holding that as the government did not appear the said suit, the decree is also binding upon it in failing to notice that after the decision of the Land Appeal Board dated 29th October, 1991, Annexure-6, which was approved by the Government declaring that the property is not abandoned property, the government had no interest in the disputed property. The High Court Division fell in an error in failing to consider that this judgment would in no way affect the appellant's title in the disputed property. 

10. According to Mr. Bhuiyan, the transfer of the disputed land in favour of the appellant Jahangir Alam is barred by section 6 of Ordinance No.LIV of 1985. If the transfer is barred by provisions of Ordinance No.LIV of 1985, then the suit is also barred by the same provision. It has been provided in section 6 amongst others that no suit or any other legal proceedings shall lie before any Court for declaration that a building is not an abandoned property etc. Mr. Bhuiyan, however, contended that section 6 will not stand in the way in maintaining the suit as framed since there is no existence of building on the disputed property and that the property in question is not included in any of the lists mentioned section 5 of the Ordinance. In elaborating his submission learned counsel tries to make out a case that in section 6, the expression "building" has been used but there is no existence of "building" in the disputed property. This submission is self contradictory, inasmuch as, if the transfer is hit by section 6 of the Ordinance, there is no reason to hold otherwise that the suit is maintainable. 

11. What is more, in paragraph 6 of the writ petition the writ petitioner stated, "Even after getting this 0.16 acre of land the petitioner Md. Shamsur Rahman Sardar constructed some valuable shops and assets upon the land by huge expenditure of money and man power." The expression 'building' has been defined in section 2(a) of the Ordinance, which means "any residential or other building or structure of any kind in an urban area and includes the land adjunct thereto, and the Court yard, tank, place of worship and private burial or cremation ground appertaining to such building". From the above definition there is no gainsaying that building includes any structure in the urban area and any land adjunct thereto. There is no dispute that there are structures on the disputed land as has been admitted by the writ petitioner in the Writ petition. In view of this admitted position, there is no merit in the contention of Mr. Bhuiyan. Over and above, admittedly the property has not been enlisted in the abandoned property list in accordance with section 5 of the Ordinance. 

12. It is not clear to us how the writ petitioner is claiming right in the disputed property. In the writ petition he did not clarify as to how he acquired title in the disputed property. He stated in paragraphs 6 and 7 that he got possession of the disputed land through Court in pursuance of the judgment passed "in Civil Suit No.371 of 1991". This is totally based upon distorted fact. Abdul Wahed Sarder instituted the above suit who got ex-parte decree. The writ petitioner is neither claiming title on the basis of purchase from Abdul Wahed Sarder nor as a successor of Abdul of 1998 challenging the inaction of the government in not delivering physical possession despite the direction given by the High Court Division. The appellant did not claim any relief against the writ petitioner in Writ Petition No.165 of 1998. He has acquired no right, title and interest in the property. If he has no interest at all it, is not incumbent upon the appellant to implead him as respondent. Therefore this observation also has no basis at all. 

14. On Consideration of the facts and circumstances of the matter, we find substance in the contention of Mr. Khan that the High Court Division on misconception of law and fact made the rule absolute. 

15. The appeal is, therefore, allowed without any order as to costs. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. Civil Appeal No.271 of 2003 is disposed of in the terms of the judgment in CA No.270 of 2003. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1548 of 2003
lawyer:
Md SR Khoshnabish, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioners. 
Not represented—The Respondents.
parties:
Alauddin (Md) and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Hakim and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated June 24, 2003 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1623 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment dated June 24, 2003 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1623 of 2001. The High Court Division by the aforesaid judgment made absolute the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated January 30, 2001 of the 2nd Court of Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 56 of 2000 reversing the judgment and decree dated March 30, 2000 of the 1st Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 127 of 1999 decreeing the same. The appellate Court upon reversing the judgment of the trial Court dismissed the suit.

2. The suit was filed seeking a decree for permanent injunction in respect of the land of Plot Nos. 3/3315, 3/3317 and 3/3319 comprising 7.25 acres of land of khatian No. B/286. The decree for permanent injunction was prayed for restraining the defendants from disturbing possession of the plaintiff in the land described in the schedule attached to the plaint.

3. Facts averring which the suit was filed, in short, that plaintiff No. 1 took settlement of 7.25 acres of land from Court of Wards of Bhawal Jamindar estate and that in respect of the land so taken settlement Khatian No. B/286 was opened in the name of the plaintiff No. 1, that plaintiff No. 1 upon constructing a dwelling house on the southern plot of the suit land was living there with the members of his family for long time, that rest of the land is being possessed by the plaintiff No. 1 by cultivating and planting fruit bearing trees, that plaintiff No.1 Abdul Hakim being an illiterate man was unaware of necessity of getting the land recorded in his name in SA khatian and RS khatian and, as such, SA and RS khatian in his name were not prepared in respect of the land in suit, that taking advantage of wrong record of right defendants tried to dispossess the plaintiffs and thereupon plaintiffs filed case in the Court of Magistrate under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, that defendants held threat to the plaintiffs to dispossess them from the land in suit on May 11, 1999 and that plaintiffs resisted said attempt with the assistance of the local people. Hence the suit seeking decree for permanent injunction for restraining the defendants from disturbing possession of the plaintiffs in respect of the land in suit.

4. Defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit stating, inter alia, that Abbas Ali, father of the defendant Nos. 1-3, took settlement of 14.20 acres of land of plot No. 3/4381 and 3/4382 of Khatian No. B/790 14.20 acres from the Court of Wards of Bhawal Estate in the year 1343 BS and they are in possession thereof upon constructing dwelling house in a portion and the rest by cultivating and planting fruit bearing trees, that at the time of SA survey land was correctly recorded in the name of Abbas Ali but Forest Department having had claimed the land taken settlement by Abbas Ali, he filed Title Suit No. 150 of 1976 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka seeking declaration of title and obtained decree, that appeal preferred by the Government against the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 150 of 1976 was dismissed for default on January 4, 1996. It was also the case of the defendants that 16 persons including the plaintiffs having had forcibly entered in the land taken settlement by Abbas Ali, he filed Title Suit No. 66 of 1988 seeking declaration of title and recovery of possession and the said suit was decreed ex parte on January 8, 1989, that the decree so obtained in Title Suit No. 66 of 1988 was put into execution by filing Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 and in the said execution case the defendants took delivery of possession on May 10, 1999. It was contended by the defendants that the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the land in suit.

5. The trial Court decreed the suit on the findings that the plaintiffs have proved their prima facie title in the land in suit and also their exclusive possession therein.

6. On appeal the appellate Court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that plaintiffs could not prove their case and thereupon reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed the suit. The plaintiffs as against the judgment of the appellate Court moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule. It was contended before the High Court Division on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioners that defendants did not claim the land of the plots in suit and that they claimed land of some other plots which are not the subject matter of the suit. It was also submitted that the Court of appeal below being the final Court of fact did not consider the oral evidence as regard possession of the parties in spite of the fact that in a suit for permanent injunction the question of possession is a material one.

7. On behalf of the defendant-opposite parties, it was submitted that evidence of PWs 3 and 4 clearly shows that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the land in suit. It was also submitted that in the criminal case filed by the plaintiffs, they admitted that they were dispossessed by the defendants and thus plaintiffs as are not in possession of the land in suit, the suit so filed seeking a decree for permanent injunction was not maintainable and that plaintiffs were not entitled to a decree for permanent injunction. It was lastly submitted that defendants having had obtained possession of the land in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1998 on May 10, 1999 as evidence by Exhibit-"ন" and thus, it being clear that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the land in suit, the appellate Court was quite correct in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissing the suit.

<u>8. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the findings that plaintiffs prayed for a decree for permanent injunction in respect of the land of plot Nos. 3/3315, 3/3317 and 3/3319 comprising 7.25 acres of land of khatian No. B/286, that plaintiffs in support of their claim of taking settlement of the land in suit from court of wards of Bhawal Estate submitted the amalnama (Exhibit-1), rent receipts (Exhibit-2, Exhibit-2(ka) and 2(kha) and the khatian B/286 (Exhibit-3) and the said documents clearly show that plaintiffs took settlement land of the plot Nos. 3/3315, 3/3317 and 3/3319 and thus proved their prima facie title to the land in suit. The High Court Division also observed that it was the case of the contesting defendants that their predecessor took settlement of land of plot Nos. 3/4381 and 3/4382 comprising 14.20 acres of land of khatian No. B/790 from the Court of Wards of Bhawal Jamindar Estate and thus "the defendants do not claim the suit plots, as mentioned in the schedule to the plaint. The trial Court has noticed this aspect of the pleadings of the parties and concluded that the admitted landlord, Court of Wards of Bhawal Estate granted settlement of 7.25 acres and 14.20 acres of land out of total land of 404.50 acres in respect of separate and distinct khatians and plots and there was no dispute of separate and distinct khatians and plots and there was no dispute with regard to the properties taken settlement by the plaintiffs and the predecessor of the defendants". The High Court Division has also observed that trial Court on consideration of the evidence held that plaintiffs are in exclusive possession of the land in suit and on consideration of the evidence led from the side of the defendants arrived at the finding that defendants "do, in fact, prove possession" as regard the land taken settlement by them, that on perusal of the document relating to Title Suit No. 150 of 1976 it is seen that the defendants filed the said suit relating to the land of plot Nos. 3/4381 and 3/4382 and that Title Suit No. 150 of 1976 does not relate to the land in suit, that Exhibit-"ন" certified copy of the writ of delivery of possession issued in Title Execution Case No.3 of 1998 which was filed on the basis of the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 66 of 1986 "shows that possession was delivered in respect of Plot Nos. 3/4381, 3/4382" and thereupon held that said Exhibit-"ন" clearly shows that defendants took possession of the land other than the land of the plots in suit, that khatian B/790 (Exhibit-"Kha") shows that the land taken settlement by the defendants' predecessor was recorded therein and the said khatian shows that the defendants have possession of the land of the plot listed therein and that the land so listed in Exhibit-"Kha" is not the subject matter of the suit filed by the plaintiffs.</u>

<u>9. The learned Advocate-on-Record submitted that the trial Court wrongly marked the document filed by the plaintiff as Exhibit and on the basis thereof trial Court having had passed the decree, the appellate Court was quite correct in setting aside the decree passed by the trial Court. The submission so made is of no substance, since it is seen from the evidence of PW 1 that while he deposed in support of his case, he filed the documents in question in the course of his deposition and the numbers of those mentioned in the deposition but on the conclusion of the deposition inadvertently exhibit numbers were not put on the documents so proved by PW 1. The plaintiffs having had noticed that inadvertent mistake of the Court filed an application and the trial Court on March 23, 2000 passed necessary order (order No. 45) to put the exhibit number on the documents. The application filed by the plaintiffs to put the Exhibit mark on the documents produced by the PW 1 was not opposed and thereupon exhibit numbers were noted in the documents without objection. The learned Advocate-on-Record submitted that defendants took delivery of possession of the land in suit in Execution Case No.3 of 1998 and in that state of the matter trial Court was in serious error in decreeing the suit for permanent injunction while undoubtedly because of the Exhibit-"ন" plaintiffs are not in possession. This submission is also of no merit, since the High Court Division on perusal of the Exhibit-"ন" held that the same relates to the land of plot Nos. 3/4381 and 3/4382 which are not the plots in suit. It was the case of the defendants that their predecessor took settlement of the land of plot Nos. 3/4381 and 3/4382. In that state of the matter it is clear that defendants have no claim in respect of the land of Plot Nos. 3/3315, 3/3317 and 3/3319 which are the plots in suit. In the background of the said fact we are of the view the High Court Division as well as the trial Court were quite correct in decreeing the suit which was for a decree for permanent injunction.</u>

10. In the background of the discussion made herein-above we find no substance in the petition.

Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

End.
